125: 	mb_chnl_ack_t * ack_buf = (mb_chnl_ack_t *)cmd_buf;
126: 	ipc_cmd_t     * ipc_cmd = (ipc_cmd_t *)cmd_buf;
127: 
128: 	/* chnl_cb->rx_xchg_buff == ipc_cmd->cmd_buff. MUST be true. */
129: 
130: 	if(cmd_buf->hdr.cmd & IPC_RSP_CMD_FLAG)  /* ipc rsp from other CPU. */
131: 	{
132: 		if(chnl_cb->tx_cmd_in_process == 0)	/* unsolicited ipc response. */
133: 		{
134: 			goto ipc_cmd_rx_isr_exit;
135: 		}
136: 
137: 		if(chnl_cb->tx_cmd != (cmd_buf->hdr.cmd & IPC_RSP_CMD_MASK))
138: 		{
139: 			/* un-matched rpc response. */
140: 			goto ipc_cmd_rx_isr_exit;
141: 		}
142: 
143: 		/* communication ok, function is completed. */
144: 		chnl_cb->tx_cmd_failed = 0;
145: 		chnl_cb->tx_cmd_in_process = 0;
146: 
147: 		BK_LOGD(MOD_TAG, "IPC_RSP_CMD: %d, %d, %d\r\n", cmd_buf->param1, cmd_buf->param2, cmd_buf->param3);
148: 
149: 		if(ipc_cmd->cmd_data_len > sizeof(chnl_cb->rsp_buf))
150: 		{
151: 			/* buffer insufficient, failed. */
152: 			chnl_cb->tx_cmd_failed = 1;
153: 			chnl_cb->rsp_len = 0;
154: 		}
155: 		else
156: 		{
157: 			/* returns ACK_STATE_COMPLETE, 
158: 			   so must copy data from cmd_buff in case that the buffer is released. */
159: 			if((ipc_cmd->cmd_buff != NULL) && (ipc_cmd->cmd_data_len > 0))
160: 			{
161: 				#if CONFIG_CACHE_ENABLE
162: 				flush_dcache(ipc_cmd->cmd_buff, ipc_cmd->cmd_data_len);
163: 				#endif
164: 				__DMB();
165: 				
166: 				memcpy(chnl_cb->rsp_buf, ipc_cmd->cmd_buff, ipc_cmd->cmd_data_len);
167: 
168: 				chnl_cb->rsp_len = ipc_cmd->cmd_data_len;
169: 			}
170: 			else
171: 			{
172: 				chnl_cb->rsp_len = 0;
173: 			}
174: 		}
175: 
176: 		rtos_set_semaphore(&chnl_cb->rsp_sema);
177: 
178: 		ipc_rsp_t * ipc_rsp = (ipc_rsp_t *)ack_buf;
179: 
180: 		/* it is a rsp command, nothing need to be returned. */
181: 		ipc_rsp->rsp_buff = NULL;
182: 		ipc_rsp->rsp_data_len = 0;
183: 
184: 		result = ACK_STATE_COMPLETE;
185: 
186: 		goto ipc_cmd_rx_isr_exit;
187: 	}
188: 	else
189: 	{
190: 		chnl_cb->rx_cmd = cmd_buf->hdr.cmd;
191: 		chnl_cb->rx_cmd_in_process = 1;
192: 
193: 		BK_LOGV(MOD_TAG, "IPC_CMD: %d, %d, %d\r\n", cmd_buf->param1, cmd_buf->param2, cmd_buf->param3);
194: 
195: 		if(ipc_cmd->cmd_data_len > sizeof(chnl_cb->cmd_buf))

47: 	 * the ACK) and forcibly clear it. 0 means "channel is IDLE". */

56:  *  use the CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX bit in the msg hdr.ctrl to distinguish where it is from.
57:  *  when CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX is set, it means from ack box ( MAILBOXn_BOX1 ).

184: {
185: 	bk_err_t		ret_code;

187: 	u32 int_mask = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
188: 	ret_code = bk_mailbox_send(data, src, dst, arg);
189: 	mb_chnl_exit_critical(int_mask);
190: 	
191: 	return ret_code;

194: static u8 mb_phy_chnl_tx_cmd(u8 log_chnl)
195: {
196: 	mb_phy_chnl_cmd_t	* cmd_ptr;
197: 	bk_err_t		ret_code;
198: 	u16 			chnl_type;
199: 	u8				phy_chnl_idx = GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = DST_CPU_ID;
200: 	u8				log_chnl_idx = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(log_chnl);
201: 
202: 	mb_phy_chnl_cb_t * phy_chnl_ptr;
203: 	mb_log_chnl_cb_t * log_chnl_cb_x;
204: 
205: 	if(SELF_CPU != GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl))
206: 		return 4;
207: 
208: 	if(SELF_CPU == phy_chnl_idx)  // transferred to self.
209: 		return 5;
210: 
211: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
212: 		return 3;
213: 
214: 	phy_chnl_ptr = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx];
215: 	log_chnl_cb_x = (mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)(phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_chnl_idx]);
216: 
217: 	if(log_chnl_idx >= phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx])
218: 		return 1;
219: 
220: 	phy_chnl_ptr->tx_seq++;
221: 	phy_chnl_ptr->tx_log_chnl = log_chnl;
222: 
223: 	cmd_ptr = (mb_phy_chnl_cmd_t *)&log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].chnnl_tx_buff;
224: 
225: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl = log_chnl;
226: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.tx_seq = phy_chnl_ptr->tx_seq;
227: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.ctrl  = 0;
228: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.state = 0;
229: 
230: 	phy_chnl_ptr->tx_hdr_cmd = cmd_ptr->hdr.cmd;
231: 
232: 	__DMB();
233: 	chnl_type = MB_PHY_CMD_CHNL;
234: 
235: 	mailbox_endpoint_t    dst_cpu = (mailbox_endpoint_t)(phy_chnl_idx);
236: 
237: 	ret_code = bk_mailbox_send(&log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].chnnl_tx_buff, SELF_CPU, dst_cpu, (void *)&chnl_type);
238: 
239: 	if(ret_code != BK_OK)
240: 	{
241: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_fault_cnt++;
242: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_fault_cnt |= 0x40000000;
243: 
244: 		return 2;
245: 	}
246: 
247: 	log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
248: 
249: 	s_mailbox_tx_cnt++;
250: 
251: 	if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_isr != NULL)
252: 	{
253: 		log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_isr(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].isr_param);  	/* phy_chnl is BUSY now, tx_isr will not trigger phy_chnl_start_tx. */
254: 	}
255: 
256: 	return 0;
257: }
258: 
259: static void mb_phy_chnl_rx_ack_isr(mb_phy_chnl_ack_t *ack_ptr)
260: {
261: 	u8		log_chnl;
262: 	u8		ret_code;
263: 	u8		phy_chnl_idx;
264: 	u8		log_chnl_idx;
265: 
266: 	mb_phy_chnl_cb_t * phy_chnl_ptr;
267: 	mb_log_chnl_cb_t * log_chnl_cb_x;
268: 
269: 	log_chnl = ack_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl;
270: 
271: 	phy_chnl_idx = GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = DST_CPU_ID;
272: 	log_chnl_idx = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(log_chnl);
273: 
274: 	s_mailbox_tx_ack_cnt++;
275: 
276: 	if(SELF_CPU != GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl))
277: 		return;
278: 
279: 	if(SELF_CPU == phy_chnl_idx)  // received from self.
280: 		return;
281: 
282: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
283: 		return;
284: 
285: 	phy_chnl_ptr = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx];
286: 	log_chnl_cb_x = (mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)(phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_chnl_idx]);
287: 
288: 	if(log_chnl_idx >= phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx])
289: 		return;
290: 
291: 	if( (log_chnl != phy_chnl_ptr->tx_log_chnl) ||
292: 		(ack_ptr->hdr.tx_seq != phy_chnl_ptr->tx_seq) )
293: 	{
294: 		phy_chnl_ptr->rx_fault_cnt++;
295: 		phy_chnl_ptr->rx_fault_cnt |= 0x40000000;
296: 
297: 		/* Stale / mismatched ACK. The original implementation just
298: 		 * returned here, which left phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state stuck at
299: 		 * BUSY forever and deadlocked all subsequent mb_chnl_write()
300: 		 * on this physical channel. Recover the channel and re-dispatch
301: 		 * any pending logical-channel tx so we don't lose the link. */
302: 		{
303: 			u32 int_mask_stale = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
304: 			u8  i;
305: 
306: 			phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state      = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
307: 			phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms = 0;
308: 
309: 			for (i = 0; i < phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx]; i++) {
310: 				if (log_chnl_cb_x[i].tx_state != CHNL_STATE_IDLE) {
311: 					u8 pending = CPX_LOG_CHNL_START(SELF_CPU, phy_chnl_idx) + i;
312: 					phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state      = CHNL_STATE_BUSY;
313: 					phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms = rtos_get_time();
314: 					if (mb_phy_chnl_tx_cmd(pending) != 0) {
315: 						log_chnl_cb_x[i].tx_state   = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
316: 						phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state      = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
317: 						phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms = 0;
318: 					}
319: 					break;
320: 				}
321: 			}
322: 			mb_chnl_exit_critical(int_mask_stale);
323: 		}
324: 		return;
325: 	}
326: 
327: 	if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_cmpl_isr != NULL)
328: 	{
329: 		/* clear following header members. */
330: 		ack_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl = 0;
331: 		ack_ptr->hdr.tx_seq       = 0;
332: 		ack_ptr->hdr.ctrl         = 0;
333: 
334: 		/* hdr.state, hdr.cmd these 2 members keep untouched. */
335: 
336: 		s_mailbox_tx_compl_cnt++;
337: 		log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_cmpl_isr(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].isr_param, (mb_chnl_ack_t *)ack_ptr);
338: 	}
339: 
340: 	u32 int_mask = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
341: 	for(log_chnl_idx = 0; log_chnl_idx < phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx]; log_chnl_idx++)  /* priority descended search. */
342: 	{
343: 		if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_state != CHNL_STATE_IDLE)
344: 			break;
345: 	}
346: 
347: 	if(log_chnl_idx >= phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx])
348: 	{
349: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state      = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
350: 		phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms = 0;
351: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(int_mask);
352: 		return;
353: 	}
354: 
355: 	log_chnl = CPX_LOG_CHNL_START(SELF_CPU, phy_chnl_idx) + log_chnl_idx;
356: 
357: 	/* About to dispatch the next pending tx on this physical channel:
358: 	 * refresh the busy-watchdog timestamp so its lifetime starts from
359: 	 * here rather than carrying over from the previous transaction. */
360: 	phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms = rtos_get_time();

293: static int ipc_router_send(mb_ipc_route_t *ipc_route, mb_ipc_cmd_t *ipc_cmd)
294: {
295: 	int   queue_cnt; // number of items in the queue.
296: 	int   free_cnt;

301: 	if(ipc_route->chnl_tx_queue_in_idx >= ipc_route->chnl_tx_queue_out_idx)
302: 	{
303: 		queue_cnt = ipc_route->chnl_tx_queue_in_idx - ipc_route->chnl_tx_queue_out_idx;
304: 		free_cnt  = ARRAY_SIZE(ipc_route->chnl_tx_queue) - queue_cnt;
305: 	}
306: 	else
307: 	{
308: 		free_cnt  = ipc_route->chnl_tx_queue_out_idx - ipc_route->chnl_tx_queue_in_idx;
309: 		queue_cnt = ARRAY_SIZE(ipc_route->chnl_tx_queue) - free_cnt;
310: 	}
311: 	
312: 	if( free_cnt <= 1 )  // reserved one for empty judgement.
313: 	{

315: 		
316: 		return  IPC_ROUTE_QUEUE_FULL;

196: static void mbox_process_desc(void)
197: {
198:   struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc;
199:   int ret;
200: 
201:   /* ACK and RESET never need ACK slots.  Process them ahead of a deferred
202:    * ordinary command, then retry ordinary commands in original FIFO order.
203:    */
204: 
205:   while ((desc = mbox_oldest_desc(true)) != NULL)
206:     {
207:       g_processing_order = desc->order;
208:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
209:       g_processing_order = 0;
210:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
211:         {
212:           g_stats.descriptor_deferred++;
213:           break;
214:         }
215: 
216:       desc->used = false;
217:     }
218: 
219:   while ((desc = mbox_oldest_desc(false)) != NULL)
220:     {
221:       g_processing_order = desc->order;
222:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
223:       g_processing_order = 0;
224:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
225:         {
226:           break;
227:         }
228: 
229:       desc->used = false;
230:     }

233: static int bk7258_mbox_irq(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
234: {
235:   uintptr_t rdata0;
236:   uintptr_t rdata1;
237:   uintptr_t sidreg;
238:   int cpu = up_cpu_index();
239:   unsigned int budget = MBOX_IRQ_DRAIN_BUDGET;
240: 
241:   (void)irq;
242:   (void)context;
243:   (void)arg;
244: 
245:   mbox_clear_errors(cpu);
246:   if (cpu == 1 && bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() >=
247:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ACK &&
248:                   bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() <
249:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_ENTER)
250:     {
251:       bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_ENTER);
252:     }
253:   sidreg = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_SID : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_SID;
254:   rdata0 = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_RDATA0 : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_RDATA0;
255:   rdata1 = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_RDATA1 : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_RDATA1;
256: 
257:   while ((bk7258_mbox_rx_status() & 2u) == 0 && budget-- != 0)
258:     {
259:       struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc;
260:       uint32_t address;
261:       uint32_t length;
262:       uint8_t source;
263: 
264:       if (cpu == 0)
265:         {
266:           mbox_process_desc();
267:         }
268: 
269:       desc = cpu == 0 ? mbox_alloc_desc() : NULL;
270:       if (cpu == 0 && desc == NULL)
271:         {
272:           g_stats.descriptor_full++;
273:           mbox_trace_errors();
274:           break;
275:         }
276: 
277:       source = getreg32(sidreg) & 0x0fu;
278:       address = getreg32(rdata0);
279:       length = getreg32(rdata1);
280: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
281:       if (length == 0)
282:         {
283:           if (source == (uint8_t)(2 - cpu))
284:             {
285:               if (cpu == 1 && address == BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK)
286:                 {
287:                   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_RAW);
288:                 }
289: 
290:               bk7258_smp_ipi_receive(irq, context, address);
291:             }
292:           else
293:             {
294:               if (cpu == 0)
295:                 {
296:                   g_stats.bad_source++;
297:                   mbox_trace_errors();
298:                 }
299:             }
300: 
301:           continue;
302:         }
303: #endif
304: 
305:       if (cpu != 0)
306:         {
307:           continue;
308:         }
309: 
310:       if (!mbox_valid_envelope(source, address, length))
311:         {
312:           continue;
313:         }
314: 
315:       __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
316:       memcpy(&desc->message, (const void *)(uintptr_t)address,
317:              sizeof(desc->message));
318:       desc->order = ++g_rx_order;
319:       desc->used = true;
320:       g_stats.rx_messages++;
321:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, desc->message.header);
322:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, address);
323:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, g_stats.rx_messages);
324:       mbox_process_desc();
325:     }
326: 
327:   if (cpu == 0)
328:     {
329:       mbox_process_desc();
330:     }
331: 
332:   if (cpu == 1 && bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() ==
333:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_RAW)
334:     {
335:       bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_EXIT);
336:     }
337: 
338:   return OK;
339: }

608: /*

615: bk_err_t mb_chnl_init(void)
616: {
617: 	bk_err_t		ret_code;
618: 	int				i, j;
619: 
620: 	mb_log_chnl_cb_t * log_chnl_cb_x;
621: 
622: 	/*
623: 	 * mb_chnl_init() is reached from mb_chnl_open(), which is called by
624: 	 * many subsystems (shell log forwarding, ipc_init, mb_uart, ...).
625: 	 * Each one of those callers runs on its own FreeRTOS task and they
626: 	 * can race here:
627: 	 *
628: 	 *   Task A: enters mb_chnl_open(MB_CHNL_LOG), sees mb_chnnl_init_ok==0,
629: 	 *           enters mb_chnl_init(), runs all the memset's, sets
630: 	 *           mb_chnnl_init_ok=1, returns. Caller then sets
631: 	 *           log_chnl_cb2[15].in_used=1 and installs rx_isr.
632: 	 *   Task B (preempted in the middle of mb_chnl_open before the
633: 	 *           init_ok check finishes): comes back, sees init_ok still
634: 	 *           == 0 (because it sampled before A set it), enters
635: 	 *           mb_chnl_init() AGAIN, and the memset wipes the
636: 	 *           log_chnl_cb_x[] array that A just populated.
637: 	 *

369: static void pwc_rx(const void *raw)
370: {
371:   const uint8_t *bytes = raw;
372:   struct pwc_message message;
373:   unsigned int next;
374: 
375:   if (bytes == NULL)
376:     {
377:       return;
378:     }
379: 
380:   /* The logical mailbox invokes PWC callbacks while holding the driver lock.
381:    * Keep the queue update in that critical section instead of recursively
382:    * acquiring the non-recursive SMP spinlock here. */
383: 
384:   next = (g_head + 1u) % PM_QUEUE_DEPTH;
385:   if (next == g_tail)
386:     {
387:       return;
388:     }
389: 
390:   message.header = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[0];
391:   message.param1 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[1];
392:   message.param2 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[2];
393:   message.param3 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[3];
394:   g_queue[g_head] = message;
395:   g_head = next;
396:   nxsem_post(&g_pwc_sem);
397: }

402: 
403:   (void)argc;

1359:       bool queued;

1363:       queued = g_channels[index].queued;
1364:       result = g_channels[index].result;
1365:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1366:       if (!queued)
1367:         {
1368:           return result == -EINPROGRESS ? OK : result;
1369:         }
1370: 
1371:       if ((int32_t)(clock_systime_ticks() - deadline) >= 0)
1372:         {

1381:        * ACK while AP remains asleep waiting for an IRQ-side drain. */

1383:       nxsig_usleep(1000);
1384:     }

212: {
213: 	u8 dst;
214: 
215: 	u32 flags = rtos_disable_int();
216: 	for (dst = 0; dst < MBOX_CHNL_NUM; dst++)

218: 		if (dst != MAILBOX_CPU0)

224: 	while (1)

226: 		mbox0_rx_desc_t desc;

228: 
229: 		flags = rtos_disable_int();
230: 		if (!rx_count)
231: 		{

234: 		}

236: 		if (!selected)

238: 		if (!selected ||
239: 			(((selected->data.param0 >> 12) & MBOX0_CTRL_ACK_BOX) == 0 &&

242: 			rtos_enable_int(flags);

244: 		}

246: 		selected->used = 0;

248: 		rtos_enable_int(flags);
249: 		if (mailbox_callback[desc.source])
250: 			mailbox_callback[desc.source](&desc.data);

254: 		rtos_enable_int(flags);

258: static void mbox0_rx_isr(mbox0_message_t *msg)
259: {
260: 	u32 address;
261: 	u32 source;
262: 	u32 reaped = 0;
263: 	mbox0_rx_desc_t *desc;
264: 	u8 ctrl;
265: 	u8 i;
266: 
267: 	if (!msg)
268: 		return;
269: 
270: 	source = msg->src_cpu;
271: 	if (source != MAILBOX_CPU1)
272: 	{
273: 		adapter_diag.bad_sid++;
274: 		return;
275: 	}
276: 	if (msg->data[1] != sizeof(mailbox_data_t))
277: 	{
278: 		adapter_diag.bad_length++;
279: 		return;
280: 	}
281: 
282: 	address = msg->data[0];
283: 	if (address & 0x3u)
284: 	{
285: 		adapter_diag.bad_alignment++;
286: 		return;
287: 	}
288: 	if (address > UINT32_MAX - sizeof(mailbox_data_t) ||
289: 		address < MBOX0_AP_RAM_START ||
290: 		address + sizeof(mailbox_data_t) > MBOX0_AP_RAM_END)
291: 	{
292: 		adapter_diag.bad_address++;
293: 		return;
294: 	}
295: 	if (rx_count >= MBOX0_RX_DESC_NUM)
296: 	{
297: 		adapter_diag.descriptor_overflow++;
298: 		return;
299: 	}
300: 
301: #if CONFIG_CACHE_ENABLE
302: 	SCB_InvalidateDCache_by_Addr((void *)address, sizeof(mailbox_data_t));
303: #endif
304: 	__DMB();
305: 	desc = NULL;
306: 	for (i = 0; i < MBOX0_RX_DESC_NUM; i++)
307: 	{
308: 		if (!rx_desc[i].used)
309: 		{
310: 			desc = &rx_desc[i];
311: 			break;
312: 		}
313: 	}
314: 	if (!desc)
315: 	{
316: 		adapter_diag.descriptor_overflow++;
317: 		return;
318: 	}
319: 	memcpy(&desc->data, (void *)address, sizeof(desc->data));
320: 	adapter_diag.last_rx_header = desc->data.param0;
321: 	ctrl = (desc->data.param0 >> 12) & 0x0f;
322: 	if (ctrl == 0)
323: 	{
324: 		/* AP serializes ordinary logical commands.  Receiving the next one
325: 		 * proves that it copied the preceding CP transport ACK, providing an
326: 		 * exact lifetime fence even during a continuous UART/PWC burst. */
327: 		for (i = 0; i < MBOX0_ACK_SLOT_NUM; i++)
328: 		{
329: 			reaped += mailbox_slots[source].ack_used[i] != 0;
330: 			mailbox_slots[source].ack_used[i] = 0;
331: 		}
332: 		adapter_diag.tx_reaped += reaped;
333: 	}
334: 	desc->source = source;
335: 	desc->order = ++rx_order;
336: 	desc->used = 1;
337: 	rx_count++;
338: 	adapter_diag.rx_accepted++;
339: 
340: }

372: bk_err_t bk_mailbox_send(mailbox_data_t *data, mailbox_endpoint_t src,
373: 			 mailbox_endpoint_t dst, void *arg)
374: {
375: 	mbox0_message_t message;
376: 	mbox0_stable_slot_t *slot;
377: 	uint32_t fifo_status;
378: 	u8 ctrl;
379: 	u8 kind = 0;
380: 	u8 index = 0;
381: 	int ret_code;
382: 
383: 	(void)arg;
384: 	if (src != MAILBOX_CPU0 || dst >= MBOX_CHNL_NUM)
385: 		return BK_ERR_MAILBOX_SRC_DST;
386: 	if (!data)
387: 		return BK_ERR_NULL_PARAM;
388: 
389: 	ret_code = mbox0_drv_get_send_stat(dst, &fifo_status);
390: 	if (ret_code != MBOX0_HAL_OK)
391: 		return BK_ERR_MAILBOX_SRC_DST;
392: 	if (fifo_status & RX_FIFO_STAT_FULL)
393: 		return BK_ERR_MAILBOX_TIMEOUT;
394: 
395: 	ctrl = (data->param0 >> 12) & 0x0f;
396: 	mbox0_reap_slots(dst);
397: 	slot = mbox0_alloc_slot(dst, ctrl, &kind, &index);
398: 	if (!slot)
399: 	{
400: 		adapter_diag.tx_slot_busy++;
401: 		return BK_ERR_BUSY;
402: 	}
403: 
404: 	memset(slot, 0, sizeof(*slot));
405: 	memcpy(&slot->data, data, sizeof(slot->data));
406: 	mailbox_slots[dst].fifo_empty_since_ms = 0;
407: #if CONFIG_CACHE_ENABLE
408: 	SCB_CleanDCache_by_Addr((u32 *)slot, sizeof(*slot));
409: #endif
410: 	__DMB();
411: 	message.data[0] = (u32)&slot->data;
412: 	message.data[1] = sizeof(slot->data);
413: 	message.dest_cpu = dst;
414: 	ret_code = mbox0_drv_send_message(&message);
415: 	if (ret_code != MBOX0_HAL_OK)
416: 	{
417: 		mbox0_release_slot(dst, kind, index);
418: 		return BK_ERR_MAILBOX_NOT_INIT;
419: 	}
420: 	if (ctrl == MBOX0_CTRL_ACK_BOX)
421: 	{
422: 		adapter_diag.last_ack_header = slot->data.param0;
423: 		adapter_diag.ack_sent++;
424: 	}
425: 	return BK_OK;
426: }

428: void bk_mailbox_tx_complete(mailbox_endpoint_t dst)
429: {
430: 	mbox0_tx_slots_t *slots;
431: 	u32 completed_order;
432: 	u8 i;
433: 
434: 	if (dst >= MBOX_CHNL_NUM)
435: 		return;
436: 	slots = &mailbox_slots[dst];
437: 	if (!slots->cmd_active)
438: 		return;
439: 	completed_order = slots->cmd_order[slots->cmd_active - 1];
440: 	for (i = 0; i < MBOX0_ACK_SLOT_NUM; i++)
441: 	{
442: 		if (slots->ack_used[i] && slots->ack_order[i] < completed_order)
443: 			slots->ack_used[i] = 0;
444: 	}
445: 	for (i = 0; i < MBOX0_CMD_SLOT_NUM; i++)
446: 	{
447: 		if (slots->cmd_used[i] && slots->cmd_order[i] <= completed_order)
448: 			slots->cmd_used[i] = 0;
449: 	}
450: 	if (slots->reset_used && slots->reset_order < completed_order)
451: 		slots->reset_used = 0;
452: 	if (slots->sync_used && slots->sync_order < completed_order)
453: 		slots->sync_used = 0;
454: 	slots->cmd_active = 0;
455: }

125: {
126: 	u32		result = ACK_STATE_FAIL;

131:

133: 	{
134: 		if(chnl_cb->tx_cmd_in_process == 0)	/* unsolicited ipc response. */
135: 		{
136: 			goto ipc_cmd_rx_isr_exit;
137: 		}
138: 
139: 		if(chnl_cb->tx_cmd != (cmd_buf->hdr.cmd & IPC_RSP_CMD_MASK))
140: 		{
141: 			/* un-matched rpc response. */
142: 			goto ipc_cmd_rx_isr_exit;
143: 		}
144: 
145: 		/* communication ok, function is completed. */
146: 		chnl_cb->tx_cmd_failed = 0;
147: 		chnl_cb->tx_cmd_in_process = 0;
148: 
149: 		BK_LOGD(MOD_TAG, "IPC_RSP_CMD: %d, %d, %d\r\n", cmd_buf->param1, cmd_buf->param2, cmd_buf->param3);
150:

153: 			/* buffer insufficient, failed. */
154: 			chnl_cb->tx_cmd_failed = 1;
155: 			chnl_cb->rsp_len = 0;
156: 		}
157: 		else
158: 		{
159: 			/* returns ACK_STATE_COMPLETE, 
160: 			   so must copy data from cmd_buff in case that the buffer is released. */
161: 			if((ipc_cmd->cmd_buff != NULL) && (ipc_cmd->cmd_data_len > 0))
162: 			{
163: 				#if CONFIG_CACHE_ENABLE
164: 				flush_dcache(ipc_cmd->cmd_buff, ipc_cmd->cmd_data_len);
165: 				#endif

168: 				memcpy(chnl_cb->rsp_buf, ipc_cmd->cmd_buff, ipc_cmd->cmd_data_len);

170: 				chnl_cb->rsp_len = ipc_cmd->cmd_data_len;
171: 			}
172: 			else
173: 			{
174: 				chnl_cb->rsp_len = 0;
175: 			}
176: 		}
177: 
178: 		rtos_set_semaphore(&chnl_cb->rsp_sema);
179: 
180: 		ipc_rsp_t * ipc_rsp = (ipc_rsp_t *)ack_buf;
181: 
182: 		/* it is a rsp command, nothing need to be returned. */
183: 		ipc_rsp->rsp_buff = NULL;
184: 		ipc_rsp->rsp_data_len = 0;
185: 
186: 		result = ACK_STATE_COMPLETE;
187: 
188: 		goto ipc_cmd_rx_isr_exit;
189: 	}
190: 	else
191: 	{
192: 		chnl_cb->rx_cmd = cmd_buf->hdr.cmd;
193: 		chnl_cb->rx_cmd_in_process = 1;
194: 
195: 		BK_LOGV(MOD_TAG, "IPC_CMD: %d, %d, %d\r\n", cmd_buf->param1, cmd_buf->param2, cmd_buf->param3);
196:

213:

215: 			}

**Conclusion**

`ipc_send_power_up()` and `ipc_send_heart_beat()` use the legacy HW-control command protocol, not Armino’s socket IPC protocol and not the newer OpenVela PWC heartbeat. The smallest compatible AP implementation only needs the existing OpenVela BK7258 logical mailbox transport, two command constructors, one stable 4-byte shared payload, and caller serialization. Porting `mb_ipc.c`, `bk_api_ipc.c`, routing tables, socket APIs, or RPC is unnecessary.

**Exact 16-Byte Record**

The hardware FIFO carries only `{address, length}`: the legacy adapter publishes the address of a stable 16-byte `mailbox_data_t` and length `16` ([mbox0_adapter.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_adapter.c:117)); MBOX0 itself has only two 32-bit data registers ([mbox0_hal.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/common/hal/mbox0_hal.c:62)). `mailbox_data_t` is four words ([mailbox_types.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/mailbox_types.h:64)).

The referenced little-endian 16-byte record is:

```text
offset  size  value
0x00    4     physical header:
                bits  7:0  command
                bits 11:8  state
                bits 15:12 control
                bits 23:16 sequence
                bits 31:24 logical channel
0x04    4     32-bit shared payload address
0x08    2     payload length
0x0a    1     unused/padding; zero in a clean implementation
0x0b    1     unused/padding; zero in a clean implementation
0x0c    4     unused for command; ACK state on legacy ACK
```

The physical header definition is explicit at [mailbox_channel.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mailbox_channel.c:64). The inner IPC overlay is `{mb_chnl_hdr_t, void *, u16}` over a 16-byte mailbox command ([mb_ipc_cmd.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_cmd.c:47)). This assumes the existing 32-bit ARM ABI: `sizeof(void *) == 4`.

For the two calls, before transport adds sequence/channel framing:

```text
power-up: word0=0x00000001, word1=0,          word2=0, word3=0
heartbeat: word0=0x00000002, word1=payload32, word2=4, word3=0
```

On transmission, word 0 becomes:

```c
command | (state << 8) | (control << 12) |
(sequence << 16) | (logical_channel << 24)
```

Thus a normal AP-to-CP power-up is `0x10SS0001`, and heartbeat is `0x10SS0002`, where `SS` is the nonzero wrapping 8-bit transport sequence. The original implementation leaves bytes `0x0a..0x0f` partly uninitialized because `ipc_cmd_t` is not zero-initialized ([mb_ipc_cmd.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_cmd.c:395)); a replacement should deliberately zero all 16 bytes.

**IDs And Direction**

The command enum is zero-based: test `0`, CPU1 power-up `1`, CPU1 heartbeat `2`, get-rate `3`, set-rate `4` ([mb_ipc_cmd.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_cmd.h:25)). The send functions use exactly commands `1` and `2` ([mb_ipc_cmd.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_cmd.c:813)).

Logical channel encoding is `dst[7:6] | src[5:4] | index[3:0]` ([mailbox_channel.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:32)). AP is logical CPU1 and opens `MB_CHNL_HW_CTRL = 0x10`, meaning CPU1 to CPU0, channel index 0 ([mailbox_channel.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:53)). CP is CPU0 and locally opens `MB_CHNL_HW_CTRL = 0x40`, meaning CPU0 to CPU1, index 0 ([mailbox_channel.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:49)). Incoming `0x10` and local `0x40` both select CP’s peer-CPU1 channel table at index 0; they are directional encodings of the same logical service.

Do not substitute the current PWC IDs. `PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD=0x05` and `PM_OPENVELA_HEARTBEAT_CMD=0x12` are separate commands on PWC channel `0x12` ([pwr_clk.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/pwr_clk.h:25)).

**Shared Buffer**

Legacy IPC advertises a 128-byte exchange buffer per direction ([mb_chnl_buff.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/mb_chnl_buff.h:28)), but these two calls need only four payload bytes. Power-up has no payload. Heartbeat writes its `u32 param` into the AP HW-control TX exchange buffer, publishes that address, and uses length `4` ([mb_ipc_cmd.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_cmd.c:379)).

The full original layout reserves four channel entries, each with two 128-byte host-TX and two host-RX buffers ([mb_chnl_buff.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_chnl_buff.c:30)). AP’s SMP configuration gives `SYSTEM_CPU_NUM=CONFIG_CPU_CNT+1=3`; CP uses `CONFIG_CPU_CNT=3`, so both calculate 512 bytes per entry and exactly 2048 bytes total ([AP config](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app/ap/config/bk7258_ap/config:13), [CP config](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app/cp/config/bk7258/config:11)).

With the current documented SWAP base `0x2809f800`, AP CPU1’s HW-control TX payload is `host_rx_buff[0]`, offset `0x100`, therefore `0x2809f900`. The current OpenVela header reserves SWAP `0x2809f800..0x2809ffff` and separately uses `0x2809fc00/0x2809fd00` for UART ([bk7258_mbox.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/hardware/bk7258_mbox.h:99)). Reserve or assert ownership of `0x2809f900..0x2809f97f`; do not merely hard-code it without checking the final linker map.

The payload must remain valid until CP has copied it and its matching ACK has completed. It must be CP-addressable, 4-byte aligned, and either non-cacheable or explicitly cleaned before send. A stack variable is invalid.

**Initialization And ACK**

Original initialization is lazy but complete: allocate two semaphores, obtain exchange buffers, open HW-control, and register RX plus TX-completion callbacks ([mb_ipc_cmd.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_cmd.c:309)). `mb_chnl_open()` initializes hardware, registers peer callbacks, and sends a reset record ([mailbox_channel.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mailbox_channel.c:670)). Driver startup also calls `ipc_init()` explicitly ([driver.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/common/driver.c:335)).

CP copies the payload before ACK and dispatches commands `1/2`; power-up calls `mb_ipc_power_on_notify()`, while heartbeat calls `mb_ipc_heartbeat_notify()` and accepts any four-byte parameter ([mb_ipc_cmd.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_cmd.c:650)).

CP mutates the received 16-byte copy into an ACK, preserving command/sequence/channel, setting control `ACK_BOX=1`, and sending it back ([mailbox_channel.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mailbox_channel.c:489)). Legacy command completion is `ACK_STATE_COMPLETE=2`, placed in word 3 ([mailbox_channel.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:128)). AP matches command and transport metadata, rejects communication-fail or `ACK_STATE_FAIL`, and wakes the waiter ([mb_ipc_cmd.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_cmd.c:238)).

**Concurrency And Timing**

`ipc_send_cmd()` serializes every HW-control caller through a binary semaphore, permits only one outstanding command, and waits forever to acquire ownership ([mb_ipc_cmd.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_cmd.c:373)). It then waits up to `600 ms` for ACK ([mb_ipc_cmd.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_cmd.c:406)). The physical layer also serializes one active transaction per destination and matches ACK channel plus sequence ([mailbox_channel.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mailbox_channel.c:259)).

The AP heartbeat task sends power-up once, then delays 2000 ms and sends heartbeat repeatedly ([mb_ipc_heartbeat.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_heartbeat.c:341)). Because each send blocks for ACK, the effective heartbeat interval is `2000 ms + mailbox completion time`, or up to about `2600 ms` after a lost ACK. Return values are ignored.

CP’s default timeout is 6000 ms, allowing three nominal intervals, unless watchdog configuration replaces it with `CONFIG_INT_WDT_PERIOD_MS` ([mb_ipc_heartbeat.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_heartbeat.c:30)). Startup waits in 2-second increments for power-up, with up to four waits in this CP version ([mb_ipc_heartbeat.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_heartbeat.c:252)). Low-voltage wake and PM sleep state suppress false timeout once by resetting the timestamp ([mb_ipc_heartbeat.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_heartbeat.c:143)).

**Current OpenVela APIs**

The generic vendor headers still expose Armino-style `bk_mailbox_init`, callback registration, and `bk_mailbox_send` ([mailbox.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/vendor_beken/chips/bk7236n/bk_idk/armino_as_lib/include/driver/mailbox.h:45)), plus the much larger socket IPC API ([mb_ipc.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/vendor_beken/chips/bk7236n/bk_idk/armino_as_lib/include/driver/mb_ipc.h:89)). Those headers are under the BK7236N vendor library and do not justify importing the BK7258 Armino stack.

The active BK7258 OpenVela implementation already provides the required lower layer: a statically asserted 16-byte compatible record, logical send API, RX registration, and completion callback ([bk7258_mbox.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/hardware/bk7258_mbox.h:122)). It transports a stable AP-RAM record as `{address, 16}` ([bk7258_mailbox_channel.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:240)), validates ACK command/channel/sequence ([bk7258_mailbox_channel.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:569)), and exposes `bk7258_mailbox_wait_hw_control()` ([bk7258_mailbox_channel.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1387)).

Its required startup sequence already occurs: logical init and physical start in serial initialization ([bk7258_serial.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_serial.c:220)); workers and link-ready probe before PWC startup ([bk7258_bringup.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:56)).

**Smallest Compatible AP Design**

Implement only a mutex-protected helper around `bk7258_mailbox_send_wire(0x10, ...)` and `bk7258_mailbox_wait_hw_control(600)`. Zero the full record. For power-up use command `1`, address/length zero. For heartbeat, write the parameter to the reserved stable word at the negotiated HW-control TX location, clean cache if required, issue a full memory barrier, use command `2`, pointer to that word, and length `4`.

Call it only after `bk7258_mailbox_link_ready()`; the current send API otherwise returns `-ENOLINK` ([bk7258_mailbox_channel.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1148)). Keep one mutex across record preparation, send, and wait so another HW-control user cannot replace the shared payload or consume the channel result between the asynchronous send and separate wait.

Do not register a second physical mailbox callback, reinitialize MBOX0, implement socket ports, or duplicate sequence/ACK logic. Also do not run both this legacy heartbeat and the existing OpenVela PWC heartbeat unless CP intentionally supports both; the current implementation already sends PWC heartbeat `0x12` every 2 seconds ([bk7258_pm_pwc.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:303)). The legacy helper is warranted only when exact `ipc_send_power_up()`/`ipc_send_heart_beat()` ABI compatibility is required.
